understanding.goal_understanding: Progress through KA59’s levels by positioning every selectable piece onto goal tiles marked '+' at the same time; if a level has multiple goals, all must be occupied simultaneously to trigger WIN and ultimately complete the full set of levels.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Each turn you control one currently selected piece (shown as 'P' in the semantic grid) and can move it one grid cell per action in the four cardinal directions, where grid cells correspond to 3x3 pixel steps in the reported [x,y] coordinates. Movement can be blocked by walls ('#') or other objects, though the movement_blocked flags are only hints and don’t perfectly predict success. Some objects (blocks 'B') are pushable: if adjacent in the direction of movement, they may be pushed along with the selected piece if space permits. Levels can contain multiple selectable pieces ('S'); you switch control by using CLICK on the exact pixel coordinates of another selectable’s position (matching the coordinates system used in player.position and objects lists), after which movement commands apply to the newly selected piece.

understanding.goal_understanding: Progress through KA59’s levels by positioning every selectable piece onto goal tiles marked '+' at the same time; if a level has multiple goals, all must be occupied simultaneously to trigger WIN and ultimately complete the full set of levels.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Each turn you control one currently selected piece (shown as 'P' in the semantic grid) and can move it one grid cell per action in the four cardinal directions, where grid cells correspond to 3x3 pixel steps in the reported [x,y] coordinates. Movement can be blocked by walls ('#') or other objects, though the movement_blocked flags are only hints and don’t perfectly predict success. Some objects (blocks 'B') are pushable: if adjacent in the direction of movement, they may be pushed along with the selected piece if space permits. Levels can contain multiple selectable pieces ('S'); you switch control by using CLICK on the exact pixel coordinates of another selectable’s position (matching the coordinates system used in player.position and objects lists), after which movement commands apply to the newly selected piece.
